title_en: Fu Jinhua v. Lü Qiubai, Liu Jianfeng — dispute over third-party objection to enforcement
ruling_gist_en: According to the Property Law of the PRC, as a general principle, registration is the constitutive requirement for the validity of changes in real property rights. The agreement on the ownership of immovable property in a divorce agreement signed by both spouses does not directly effect a change in real property rights. One party may only assert a contractual obligation against the other party based on a claim right (creditor's right) to perform the registration of the change in property ownership. Where the property owner has not been changed in accordance with the law, the agreement on the ownership of immovable property in the divorce agreement does not have the legal effect of opposing external third-party claims.
keywords_en: Civil; Third-party's objection to enforcement action; First instance; Intermediate People's Court; Shanghai; Natural person; Property Law; Marriage Law; Real property effect of ownership in divorce agreement; Whether failure to complete change registration can oppose enforcement; Dismissal of claims; Divorce agreement; Ownership of immovable property; Failure to complete transfer registration; Objection to enforcement; Principle of public notice of real property rights; Real property rights; Divorce; Equity transfer
full_text_en:
Fu Jinhua v. Lü Qiubai and Liu Jianfeng — action of objection to execution by a third party

Ruling Summary

Under the Property Law of the PRC, the acquisition, transfer, and extinction of real property rights generally take effect upon registration as a necessary condition. A divorce agreement between spouses regarding the attribution of real property does not directly produce the effect of a change in property rights. One party may only claim against the other party for performance of the contractual obligation to register the transfer of the property title based on a right of claim in personam. Where the real property title has not been legally altered, the provisions on the attribution of real property in a divorce agreement are not effective against the claims of external third-party creditors.

Plaintiff: Fu Jinhua, female, 47 years old, Han Chinese, residing in Songjiang District, Shanghai.

Defendant: Lü Qiubai, male, 48 years old, resident of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the PRC, residing in Minhang District, Shanghai.

Third Party: Liu Jianfeng, male, 52 years old, Han Chinese, residing in Tongxiang City, Zhejiang Province.

Plaintiff Fu Jinhua brought an action against Defendant Lü Qiubai and Third Party Liu Jianfeng regarding a dispute over an objection to execution by a third party, before the Shanghai No. 1 Intermediate People's Court.

Plaintiff Fu Jinhua alleged: The plaintiff and Third Party Liu Jianfeng registered their marriage in October 1989. After marriage, in 2000, they purchased the house located at Room X, Lane X, No. X, Zhongshan Er Road, Songjiang District, Shanghai (hereinafter referred to as the "Zhongshan Er Road house"), and in 2003, they purchased the house located at No. X, Lane X, Beicui Road, Songjiang District, Shanghai (hereinafter referred to as the "Beicui Road house"). The parties registered their divorce on October 29, 2007, and in the divorce agreement, they agreed that the ownership of both houses would belong to the plaintiff. However, to reduce mortgage loan refinancing fees and defer the payment of transaction deed tax, the parties did not immediately go through the formalities for the transfer of real property title. After the divorce, the plaintiff continued to reside in the said Zhongshan Er Road house. Because the third party and Defendant Lü Qiubai had a dispute over equity transfer in 2012 and sued, the defendant applied to the court for enforcement based on the effective legal document, Civil Judgment (2012) Hu Yi Zhong Min Si (Shang) Chu Zi No. S51. The court seized the Zhongshan Er Road house registered in the name of the judgment debtor Liu Jianfeng and the Beicui Road house registered in the names of the plaintiff and the third party. The plaintiff raised an objection to execution with the enforcement division of that case, which was dismissed by ruling. The plaintiff argued that, although the title to the said houses had not yet been transferred and registered solely in the plaintiff's name, there was sufficient evidence to prove that the plaintiff had lawful property rights to the said two properties. The third party's debt to the defendant was a personal debt incurred after the divorce between the plaintiff and the third party. The plaintiff was merely a third party in the enforcement case. Therefore, the plaintiff requested the court to rule: 1. Confirm that the ownership of the house at Zhongshan Er Road, Songjiang District, Shanghai, and the house at Beicui Road, Songjiang District, Shanghai, belongs to the plaintiff; 2. Lift the judicial seizure of the said two real properties and cease enforcement against them.

Defendant Lü Qiubai argued: The agreement between Plaintiff Fu Jinhua and Third Party Liu Jianfeng in the divorce agreement cannot contravene the provisions of Articles 9 and 14 of the Property Law. The titleholder of real property must be based on registration and cannot be altered by private agreement between the parties. Therefore, the defendant disagreed with the plaintiff's claims.

Third Party Liu Jianfeng stated that he agreed with Plaintiff Fu Jinhua's claims.

The Shanghai No. 1 Intermediate People's Court found:

During the existence of the marital relationship between Plaintiff Fu Jinhua and Third Party Liu Jianfeng, they purchased the house at Zhongshan Er Road, Songjiang District, Shanghai, and the house at Beicui Road, Songjiang District, Shanghai. Among them, the title to the Zhongshan Er Road house was registered in the third party's name, and the title to the Beicui Road house was jointly registered in the names of the plaintiff and the third party. The Beicui Road house had a bank mortgage loan, with the third party as the primary borrower.

On October 29, 2007, Plaintiff Fu Jinhua and Third Party Liu Jianfeng registered their divorce with the civil affairs authority. On October 31, 2007, the plaintiff and the third party signed a divorce agreement, stipulating: "The elder son, Liu Yang, shall be with the woman; the younger son, Liu Hai, shall be with the man; the two houses in Songjiang District, Shanghai, shall belong to the woman; the company shares shall be 21.125% for the third party, 21.125% for Liu Yang, 21.125% for Liu Hai, and 16% for the plaintiff, with Liu Yang's shares administered by the woman on his behalf." This divorce agreement is currently held by the civil affairs authority. After the signing of the said divorce agreement, the title to the houses and the company shares involved in the agreement were not changed and registered.

Third Party Liu Jianfeng obtained a marriage certificate with a third person on March 12, 2008, and on October 30, 2012, reached a divorce agreement through court mediation, which was confirmed by a civil mediation letter issued by the court.

Third Party Liu Jianfeng was involved in a dispute over equity transfer with Defendant Lü Qiubai. After trial, the court issued a Civil Judgment (2012) Hu Yi Zhong Min Si (Shang) Chu Zi No. S51 on March 27, 2013, ordering the third party to repay the defendant RMB 20,000,000 and pay corresponding interest within ten days from the effective date of the judgment, and ordering Lizhan Textile (Zhejiang) Co., Ltd. and Zhejiang Hongzhan New Materials Co., Ltd. to bear joint and several repayment liability with the third party. After the judgment became effective, because the third party and Lizhan Textile (Zhejiang) Co., Ltd. and Zhejiang Hongzhan New Materials Co., Ltd. failed to perform the repayment obligations determined by the effective judgment, the defendant applied to the court for enforcement. During the enforcement process, the court lawfully seized the said Zhongshan Er Road house and Beicui Road house.

After the said houses were seized, Plaintiff Fu Jinhua raised an objection to the enforcement division of the court, primarily on the grounds that the divorce agreement with Third Party Liu Jianfeng had already stipulated that the ownership of the two houses belonged to the plaintiff, but the formalities for title transfer had not been completed. The plaintiff requested the court to lift the seizure of the disputed houses and suspend enforcement.

The enforcement division of the court formed a collegial panel to conduct a hearing and examination according to law, and on June 19, 2014, issued Enforcement Rulings (2014) Hu Yi Zhong Zhi Yi Zi Nos. 7-1 and 7-2, dismissing the objection raised by Fu Jinhua. Plaintiff Fu Jinhua then filed the present lawsuit, requesting the court to rule as prayed.

The Shanghai No. 1 Intermediate People's Court held:

The houses in dispute in this case were purchased during the existence of the marital relationship between Plaintiff Fu Jinhua and Third Party Liu Jianfeng. According to the relevant provisions of the Marriage Law, the disputed houses should be considered as joint property of the plaintiff and the third party. Article 9 of the Property Law of the PRC clearly provides that "the creation, alteration, transfer, and extinction of real property rights shall take legal effect upon registration according to law; without registration, they shall not take legal effect." The parties' agreement in the divorce agreement that the title to the said houses all belonged to the plaintiff is a disposition by the third party of his share in the title to the disputed houses. This disposition, without a change in title registration, does not directly produce the legal effect of a change in property rights and is not effective against third parties. Because the title to the disputed houses has not been changed and registered, Third Party Liu Jianfeng remains the registered titleholder of the disputed houses, and his share of the property rights in the disputed houses has not been transferred to the plaintiff. Therefore, in the situation where the third party still has outstanding debts to external parties, Defendant Lü Qiubai, as a creditor of the third party, is legally entitled to request the judicial seizure and enforcement of the property registered in the third party's name. The plaintiff's claim, based on the provisions of the Divorce Agreement regarding the title to the disputed houses, to confirm that the ownership of the disputed houses belongs to the plaintiff and to request the lifting of the judicial seizure and cessation of enforcement against the disputed houses, lacks legal basis and is not supported by the court.

In conclusion, in accordance with Articles 6 and 9 of the Property Law of the PRC, the Shanghai No. 1 Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment on February 9, 2015:

Reject all claims of Plaintiff Fu Jinhua.

After the judgment of first instance, none of the parties filed an appeal, and the judgment of first instance has taken legal effect.
